_comment:
The whole body flinches away from something. Built on one asymmetry: the character leans IN first (0.30, eased, 4% bigger and a touch closer) and then leaves in a single un-eased frame. A move with `eased` tweens and a move without it snaps, so the recoil itself is a hard cut to the new position - that snap IS the impact - while the recovery at 2.35 is eased and slow, which is what makes it read as nerve rather than as a teleport. Between them the body settles OUT twice, not in, so it is still backing away while it looks like it is coming back.

Deliberately NOT animated: no run, no fall, no clip, no arms thrown up. The travel is whole-actor dx plus a scaleBy DOWN, which reads as retreating from camera and costs no art at all. Only `head` and `eyes` take part transforms, both ToonRigRepair guarantees. The final beat writes dx/dy 0.0 and scaleBy 1.0 explicitly - dx/dy are offsets from the bound mark and position carries to the end of the SCENE, so a recoil that forgets this leaves the character standing a stride to the left forever.

Trigger note: 'staggers back' / 'reels backward' belong to `stagger-dizzy` and are deliberately NOT claimed here. A stagger is a character who has been HIT and cannot walk straight; a recoil is a character who has SEEN something and will not go near it. Two phrases pointing at two gags is how a wrong gag fires, so this one keeps to recoil/flinch/shrink phrasing and leaves the dizzy vocabulary alone. Bare 'shrinks back' is likewise left to `shrink-in-fear`: it is a substring of that gag's own phrases, so claiming it here would swallow their sentence on index order alone.

beats._comment: rest, and a squint - leaning in to inspect whatever this is
ANTICIPATION, and it goes the WRONG WAY on purpose: in and slightly bigger. A recoil with no lean-in has nothing to recoil from. Held 0.36s - four frames at 12fps - before it is thrown away.
leads the picture by half a frame
THE RECOIL. No `eased` - this move SNAPS, and the snap is the impact. Back (dx), fractionally up off the heels (dy) and 10% smaller, which reads as away from camera without a single new drawing.
overshoot recovered - drifts back toward the mark. Feet down.
and OUT again, further than it just came in. The second thought is worse than the first; this is what stops the recovery reading as relief.
held out there with the eyes wide. A snap, on top of a body that is barely moving.
under the hold. The only thing happening for 0.9s is a pulse.
THE EASED RETURN, and the tidy-up in the same beat. Slow back to the mark it was bound to - a nervous edge back in, against a departure that took one frame.

eyes and head back to the rig's rest pose. Sits 0.20s after the eased return starts, not 0.10s - at 12fps a 0.10s gap is barely one frame, and a restore that lands on the same frame as the move before it is a restore nobody sees.
